(Capacity: 13,819) | champion = | tourney = | tourney_result = }} {{2023-24 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2023–24 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] during the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]] were led by fifth-year head coach [[Mick Cronin (basketball)|Mick Cronin]], and they played their home games at [[Pauley Pavilion]] as a member of the [[Pac-12 Conference]]. It was the Bruins' final season as a member of the Pac-12 before joining the [[Big Ten Conference]] on July 1, 2024. UCLA had seven [[freshmen]] on their roster, and eight newcomers overall,{{cite news|first=John|last=Davis|title=UCLA men’s basketball vs. Lafayette: What you need to know|date=November 9, 2023|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/11/09/ucla-mens-basketball-vs-lafayette-what-you-need-to-know/|access-date=November 11, 2023}} along with three [[sophomore]]s.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Young players fueling UCLA’s resurgence as Bruins beat Oregon in a wild one|date=February 3, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-02-03/dylan-andrews-shines-ucla-defeats-oregon-recap|access-date=February 5, 2024}} The Bruins won their first three games and started the season 5–2.{{cite news|first=John W.|last=Davis|title=Berke Buyuktuncel cleared ahead of UCLA men’s basketball vs. No. 4 Marquette: What you need to know|date=November 19, 2023|newspaper=The Orange County Register|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2023/11/19/berke-buyuktuncel-cleared-ahead-of-ucla-mens-basketball-vs-no-4-marquette-what-you-need-to-know/|access-date=January 4, 2023}}{{cite news|first=John|last=Davis|title=UCLA men’s basketball at Villanova: What you need to know|date=December 8, 2023|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/12/08/ucla-mens-basketball-at-villanova-what-you-need-to-know/|access-date=January 4, 2024}} The team was limited offensively.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Mick Cronin questions players’ aptitude after UCLA struggles during loss to Stanford|date=January 3, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-01-03/ucla-bruins-basketball-stanford-cardinal|access-date=January 4, 2024}} On January 11, 2024, they lost 90–44 to [[Utah]] for their eighth loss in nine games. The 46-point defeat was the second-worst in the program's history, behind a 48-point loss (109–61) to [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] in [[1996–97 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|1997]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA’s dismal season hits a new low in a 46-point loss to Utah|date=January 11, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-01-11/ucla-basketball-blowout-loss-utah|access-date=January 12, 2024}} On January 27, UCLA defeated [[2023–24 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]] 65–50 at the [[Galen Center]]. It was the Bruins' first win in [[UCLA–USC rivalry|their crosstown rivalry]] under Cronin on the Trojans' home court, ending a five-game losing streak at the site. For the first time since [[2003–04 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2004]], the teams faced each other both with losing records.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Dylan Andrews and Adem Bona deliver UCLA to victory over rival USC|date=January 27, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2024-01-27/dylan-andrews-adem-bona-deliver-ucla-over-usc|access-date=January 28, 2024}} UCLA beat [[2023–24 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] 71–63, dropping the Ducks to second place, for their third straight win and fifth in their last six games. They extended their winning streak to six games, and had won eight of their last nine, leading up to their rematch against Utah. However, the Bruins lost 70–69 to the Utes on a last-second basket.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Utah shocks UCLA on last-second basket, ending Bruins’ six-game winning streak|date=February 18, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-02-18/ucla-left-stunned-loss-utah-recap|access-date=February 25, 2024}} They also lost their following game to USC to fall to 14–13 overall and 9–7 in the conference, needing to win the [[2024 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]] to advance to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Sloppy defense and poor shooting plague UCLA’s starting guards in loss to rival USC|date=February 24, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2024-02-24/mick-cronin-usc-ucla-players-recruiting-fight|access-date=February 25, 2024}} UCLA lost their third game in a row, dropping back to .500 after allowing a season high in points in a 94–77 defeat to [[2023–24 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Fed up after another UCLA loss, Mick Cronin delivers stern warning to his players|date=February 29, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-02-29/ucla-basketball-loses-washington-mick-cronin|access-date=March 1, 2024}} The Bruins won their regular-season finale 59–47 at home against [[2023–24 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]] to end a five-game losing streak, including three at Pauley Pavilion.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA overcomes sluggish start with a huge scoring run in win over Arizona State|date=March 9, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-03-09/ucla-basketball-rallies-victory-arizona-state-recap|access-date=March 10, 2024}} In their Pac-12 tournament opener, Dylan Andrews scored a career-high 31 points to lead No. 5-seed UCLA to a 67–57 win over 12th-seeded [[2023–24 Oregon State Beavers men's basketball team|Oregon State]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Dylan Andrews’ hot shooting lifts UCLA to a Pac-12 tournament win over Oregon State|date=March 13, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-03-13/ucla-basketball-vs-oregon-state-recap|access-date=March 14, 2024}} The Bruins were eliminated in the following game in the quarterfinals, losing 68–66 to No. 4-seed [[2023–24 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]]. With 4.4 seconds remaining, Andrews took the inbounds pass, drove downcourt, and shot a [[floater (basketball)|floater]] inside the [[free throw line]] over [[N'Faly Dante]] as the buzzer sounded, but the ball bounced off the back of the rim.{{cite news|first=Luca|last=Evans|title=UCLA comes up short versus Oregon in Pac-12 Tournament|date=March 16, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2024/03/14/ucla-comes-up-short-versus-oregon-in-pac-12-tournament/|access-date=March 16, 2024}}{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Dylan Andrews and UCLA can’t conjure any last-second magic in season-ending loss|date=March 14, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-03-14/ucla-loses-oregon-pac-12-tournament-recap|access-date=March 16, 2024}} He ended the game with 24 points, and averaged 21.2 points over the final six games.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title='Everybody’s a free agent': UCLA is headed for what might be its wildest offseason|date=March 15, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-03-15/ucla-mens-basketball-roster-offseason-mick-cronin|access-date=March 16, 2024}} Cronin's personal streak of 12 consecutive NCAA tournament appearances ended. == Offseason == {| class="wikitable sortable sortable" style="text-align: center" |+ style="{{NCAA color cell|UCLA Bruins}}" | UCLA Departures |- align=center !
